## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Paccuppannātītavāra* is a textual unit within the *Yamaka* (Ya 5.3.4), the sixth book of the canonical Pali Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. Operating within the third subdivision of the fifth major chapter of the *Yamaka*, the text treats the temporal interplay of present and past phenomena according to the treatise's characteristic paired dialectical scheme [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral lists one translation of the text in a single language [SuttaCentral].

No external curated parallels in Chinese, Tibetan, or Sanskrit are identified by SuttaCentral, and automated cross-language searches report no significant alignments with external corpora [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali tradition, however, computational analysis by DharmaNexus documents pervasive textual reuse, identifying 260 matching passages across 19 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The highest volume of shared phrasing occurs with closely linked portions of the same chapter, notably the *Uppādavāra* (Ya 5.2.1), *Nirodhavāra* (Ya 5.2.2), *Uppādanirodhavāra* (Ya 5.2.3), *Paccuppannānāgatavāra* (Ya 5.3.5), and *Atītānāgatavāra* (Ya 5.3.6) [DharmaNexus]. In addition, substantial segments are shared with corresponding *Paccuppannātītavāra* sections in other *Yamaka* treatises (such as Ya 2.3.4, Ya 3.3.4, and Ya 10.3.4), the *Pariññāvāra* (Ya 7.2.4), and the *Abhidhammamātikāpāḷi* [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
